---
title: "Ranked values"
description: >
  Draw any ranked metric along its rank, with the top features named:
  plot_rank() for gene rankings, NES, specificity scores, reporter
  metabolites or regulon specificity.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_common.R")
```

**Question:** which features top (or end) a ranking, and how steeply does the
metric fall away from them?

| Function | Shows | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| `plot_rank()` | features along their rank (x) against a value (y), the ends of the ranking named | any rankable metric: fold changes, NES, specificity scores (e.g. SCENIC's regulon specificity), reporter metabolite z-scores |

`plot_rank()` takes any table: `rank.by` is the column the features are
ranked by, `value` the column drawn on y (by default the same). It is drawn
small (2.5 × 1.8 in panels), to fit in a corner of a figure, and its labels
are smaller than the tick labels (7 pt, less when they do not fit).

**Data:** interferon-β (IFN-β) vs control in each cell type of the PBMCs of
[Kang et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042) (pseudobulk, edgeR; see
[DE: many comparisons](de-multi.html)), and the MSigDB Hallmark gene sets.

```{r data}
de <- docs_kang_de()
names(de)
# Symbols shared by several genes carry their Ensembl ID ("CCL5_ENSG...");
# the symbol alone is shown
symbol <- function(x) sub("_ENSG[0-9]+$", "", x)
mono <- de[["CD14 Mono"]]
mono$gene <- symbol(rownames(mono))
mono$neg_log10_fdr <- -log10(mono$FDR)
```

## Rank plot

Genes of CD14 monocytes ranked by their log2 fold change, coloured by the
−log10 FDR. The fold change has both signs, so both ends are named
(`label.side = "auto"`): the most induced and the most repressed genes.

```{r rank}
plot_rank(
    mono,
    rank.by = "logFC",
    feature.col = "gene",
    color.by = "neg_log10_fdr",
    italic.genes = TRUE,
    y.title = "log2 fold change",
    legend.title = "-log10 FDR"
)
```

Each label sits next to its gene, in the corner the curve leaves empty
(towards higher ranks at the top end, lower ranks at the bottom end), clear
of the other labels, the points and the leader lines. Labels are placed for
the panel size, so set it with `panel.width` / `panel.height`.

**Ties.** Every feature gets its own position, so tied features are never
drawn on top of each other. Ties are broken by `value`, then by name (never
by the row order of the table), and the source data hold both the position
(`rank`) and the tied rank to report (`rank_tied`: 1, 2, 2, 4).

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `split.by`

One ranking per level, one panel each: here the NES of the Hallmark gene sets
in each cell type (fgsea on the signed −log10 p-value, as in
[Gene-set enrichment](enrichment.html)), three named at each end.

```{r split, fig.width = 9}
hallmark <- docs_hallmark()
hallmark_list <- split(hallmark$gene_symbol, hallmark$gs_name)
signed_p <- function(t) {
    stats <- -log10(t$PValue) * sign(t$logFC)
    sort(setNames(stats, rownames(t)), decreasing = TRUE)
}
set.seed(1)
gsea <- lapply(names(de), function(ct) {
    res <- fgsea::fgsea(
        hallmark_list,
        signed_p(de[[ct]]),
        minSize = 15,
        maxSize = 500,
        eps = 0
    )
    data.frame(
        set = sub("HALLMARK_", "", res$pathway),
        NES = res$NES,
        neg_log10_padj = -log10(res$padj),
        cell_type = ct
    )
})
gsea <- do.call(rbind, gsea)
plot_rank(
    gsea,
    rank.by = "NES",
    feature.col = "set",
    split.by = "cell_type",
    color.by = "neg_log10_padj",
    label.n = 3,
    ncol = 3,
    legend.title = "-log10 padj"
)
```

#### One-signed metric

A specificity score is never negative and only its top matters, so only the
first ranks are named. Here, a simple one (in the spirit of SCENIC's regulon
specificity score, not the same): each gene's share of its expression summed
over the six cell types (mean CPM of the cell type's pseudobulk samples), for
genes of at least 10 CPM somewhere.

```{r specificity, fig.width = 9}
genes <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(de, rownames))
cpm <- sapply(de, function(t) 2^t[genes, "logCPM"])
rownames(cpm) <- genes
cpm <- cpm[apply(cpm, 1, max) >= 10, ]
share <- cpm / rowSums(cpm)
spec <- data.frame(
    gene = rep(symbol(rownames(share)), ncol(share)),
    cell_type = rep(colnames(share), each = nrow(share)),
    share = as.vector(share)
)
plot_rank(
    spec,
    rank.by = "share",
    feature.col = "gene",
    split.by = "cell_type",
    ncol = 3,
    italic.genes = TRUE,
    y.title = "Share of expression"
)
```

#### `label = "selected"`

Named features only, wherever they rank: here interferon-stimulated genes,
coloured by whether they are DE (`color.by` with a discrete column).

```{r selected}
mono$status <- ifelse(
    mono$FDR < 0.05,
    ifelse(mono$logFC > 0, "Up", "Down"),
    "Not DE"
)
plot_rank(
    mono,
    rank.by = "logFC",
    feature.col = "gene",
    color.by = "status",
    cols = c(Down = "#174EA6", "Not DE" = "grey80", Up = "#C91F28"),
    label = "selected",
    label.features = c("ISG15", "IFIT1", "MX1", "IFI6", "OAS1"),
    italic.genes = TRUE,
    y.title = "log2 fold change"
)
```

#### Ties

A metric with many ties: in how many of the six cell types each gene is
induced (FDR < 0.05, log2 fold change > 1), with the genes of each count
ordered by their mean fold change (`value`). The tied rank to report is in
the source data.

```{r ties}
up <- sapply(de, function(t) {
    t[genes, "FDR"] < 0.05 & t[genes, "logFC"] > 1
})
breadth <- data.frame(
    gene = symbol(genes),
    n_cell_types = rowSums(up),
    mean_logfc = rowMeans(sapply(de, function(t) t[genes, "logFC"]))
)
breadth <- breadth[breadth$n_cell_types > 0, ]
p <- plot_rank(
    breadth,
    rank.by = "n_cell_types",
    value = "mean_logfc",
    feature.col = "gene",
    italic.genes = TRUE,
    y.title = "Mean log2 fold change"
)
p
src <- attr(p, "source_data")
head(src[order(src$rank), c("feature", "rank", "rank_tied", "rank_value", "value")])
```

#### `decreasing = FALSE`

Rank 1 is the smallest value, e.g. genes ranked by p-value, with their fold
change on y.

```{r increasing}
plot_rank(
    mono,
    rank.by = "PValue",
    value = "logFC",
    feature.col = "gene",
    decreasing = FALSE,
    label.side = "first",
    italic.genes = TRUE,
    x.title = "Rank by p-value",
    y.title = "log2 fold change"
)
```

## Notes

- **Which end is named.** `label.side = "auto"` names both ends of a signed
  metric (z-scores, fold changes, NES: both directions mean something) and
  the first ranks otherwise (specificity, −log10 p: the end of the ranking
  is not of interest). `"first"`, `"last"` and `"both"` choose directly.
- **Crowded panels.** When the labels do not fit at 7 pt, they are made
  smaller (to 5 pt, the same size in every panel); if they still do not fit,
  a warning suggests a smaller `label.n` or a larger panel. Long names are
  wrapped after spaces, hyphens, underscores or commas (`label.wrap`).
- **Shared colour scales.** `color.limits` fixes the colour scale, so that
  figures of several time points or conditions compare; values beyond it
  get the end colours.
